title: Semantic Crystallization
description_html:
Semantic Crystallization (SemCrys) introduces a conceptual primitive for stabilization and inspection of semantic continuity during probabilistic transformation. The paper argues that modern AI systems preserve syntax and operational coherence far more rigorously than they preserve semantic continuity, allowing hidden semantic drift to accumulate invisibly across retrieval, summarization, orchestration, and multi-agent transformation chains.

The work defines SemCrys as the stabilization of semantic anchor-reference bindings and governed relational semantics under active interpretive regimes. Rather than attempting universal semantic formalization, the paper proposes externally inspectable semantic anchoring as a partial continuity infrastructure for probabilistic systems. Central concepts include hidden oracle surfaces, governed bindings and relations, interpretive authority, continuity inspection, relational mutation, and actionable conflict surfacing.

The paper distinguishes semantic continuity from probabilistic plausibility, arguing that coherent outputs may still conceal incompatible semantic mutation across transformation steps. SemCrys is positioned not as semantic correctness infrastructure, but as semantic continuity visibility infrastructure: a framework for surfacing semantic instability before it compounds invisibly inside language systems.

The paper further explores:

  • weak semantic anchoring
  • transformation-boundary inspection
  • governed semantic projection
  • relational continuity
  • false continuity failure modes
  • temporal interpretive drift
  • and the infrastructural implications of semantic governance for long-context AI systems and multi-agent architectures

SemCrys is presented as a framing primitive rather than a finalized implementation architecture, intended to support future research into governed semantic systems, semantic continuity infrastructure, and probabilistic transformation governance.
